common_name: LA Early Satsuma (Louisiana Early Satsuma Mandarin)

planting.note: Set container-grown trees out in spring once frost danger has passed, in full sun with well-drained, slightly acidic soil; choose the warmest, most sheltered spot available for reliable zone 8b-9 performance.

directions: LA Early was selected by the LSU AgCenter citrus breeding program from open-pollinated seedlings planted in the late 1960s at the Citrus Research Station in Port Sulphur, Louisiana, and released for its unusually early ripening window. Trees are medium-sized with a spreading, drooping, thornless habit and set fruit heavily and evenly through the canopy. Fruit is medium-to-large, oblate, thin-skinned, essentially seedless, and ready to pick from early September into mid-October, well ahead of standard Owari satsuma. As with other satsumas, cold hardiness is good for citrus but root zones should be mulched and young trees protected during hard freezes in zone 8b plantings.
sources: LSU AgCenter — 'LA Early': A New Early Market Satsuma (Research Circular, 2001)

common_name: Early St. Ann Satsuma (Early-Maturing LSU AgCenter Satsuma Mandarin)

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring after the last frost, in full sun on well-drained, slightly acidic soil; site in a protected microclimate for best results at the northern edge of its range.

directions: Early St. Ann came out of the LSU AgCenter's fresh-market citrus improvement program and was released as an early-maturing satsuma bred to outperform the older Armstrong selection in fruit size, yield, and eating quality. Fruit is oblate, medium-to-large, thin-skinned with a light leathery rind and deep orange, richly flavored flesh, ripening from early September into mid-October. Trees are productive and manageable in size, making this a good choice where gardeners want fruit ahead of the main satsuma season. It shares the general cold tolerance of other satsuma mandarins but still benefits from trunk wraps or covers during hard freeze events in zone 8 plantings.
sources: LSU AgCenter — 'Early St. Ann': A New Early Maturing Satsuma Mandarin (Research Circular, 2001)
